BRIEF FACTS:
1. Succinctly, the case of the plaintiff is that the plaintiff and her husband are residing at House no.D1/C1111-A, D- Block, Gali no.1C, Ratiya Marg, Sangam Vihar, New Delhi-110080 ( hereinafter called the suit property ), being the absolute owner and in physical possession of the property and, the plaintiff has said that she purchased the suit property on 27.07.2006 through GPA, agreement to sale and purchase, affidavit,
Will, possession letter, receipt etc. and constructed the same from her own earnings/resources.

The plaintiff has further explained that defendant no.1 is her son,
who earlier got married in the year 2016 but he started harassing his ex-wife, who later filed a case against him and the others in the year 2017 and eventually, the dispute settled in the year 2020 after which defendant no.1 took divorce from her.

She further submits that in February, 2020, defendant no.1 got married to defendant no.2 and they were permitted to live in a portion of the suit property as licensees,
without making any payment but after 2 months of their marriage, both the defendants started harassing the plaintiff and her husband and in these alleged acts,
defendant no.2 was being supported by her father, brother and other family members.

As per the plaintiff, defendants and the family of defendant no.2 started pressurizing her to transfer the suit property in the name of defendant no.2, failing which they threatened to throw the plaintiff and her husband out of the suit property.
It is also alleged that in order to harass the plaintiff and her husband, defendants used to shut down the electricity at night and close the water connection and abuse and misbehave with them.

It is further alleged that defendants manhandled the plaintiff and her husband and threatened to implicate them in false cases of dowry,
domestic violence etc.

14.In order to prove these issues, the plaintiff has relied on her oral averments and Ex PW-1/1 to Ex PW-1/5.

sentences.text: 15.Now, the question arises as to whether the defendant no.1 has a right to reside in the suit property or not.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Satish Chandra Ahuja v. Sneha Ahuja, (2021) 1 SCC 414 held that:
"83.

entities.text: Satish Chandra Ahuja v. Sneha Ahuja, (2021) 1 SCC 414
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Before we close our discussion on Section 2(s), we need to observe that the right to residence under Section 19 is not an indefeasible right of residence in shared household especially when the daughter-in-law is pitted against aged father-in-law and mother- in-law.
The senior citizens in the evening of their life are also entitled to live peacefully not haunted by marital discord between their son and daughter-in-law.

While granting relief both in application under Section 12 of Act,
2005 or in any civil proceedings
, the Court has to balance the rights of both the parties.

The directions issued by High court in paragraph 56 adequately balances the rights of both the parties."
16.Further, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Vinay Varma vs Kanika Pasricha and Anr, (2019) 265 DLT 211 has set out the broad guidelines to strike a balance CS SCJ No. 1228 of 2022 AMARJEETT KAUR SOHAL VS. GURVINDER SINGH Pages 10 of 16

It was held by the Hon'ble court:
"1. The court/tribunal has to first ascertain the nature of the relationship between the parties and the son's/ daughter's family.
2. If the case involves eviction of a daughter in law, the court has to also ascertain whether the daughter-in-law was living as part of a joint family.
3. If the relationship is acrimonious, then the parents ought to be permitted to seek eviction of the son/daughter-in-law or daughter/son in-law from their premises.
In such circumstances, the obligation of the husband to maintain the wife would continue in terms of the principles under the DV Act.

4. If the relationship between the parents and the son are peaceful or if the parents are seen colluding with their son, then, an obligation to maintain and to provide for the shelter for the daughter-in-law would remain both upon the in-laws and the husband especially if they were living as part of a joint family.

In such a situation,
while parents would be entitled to seek eviction of the daughter-in-law from their property, an alternative reasonable accommodation would have to be provided to her.

sentences.text: In case the son or his family is ill-treating the parents then the parents would be entitled to seek unconditional eviction from their property so that they can live a peaceful life and also put the property to use for their generating income and for their own expenses for daily living.

6. If the son has abandoned both the parents and his own wife/children, then if the sons family was living as part of a joint family prior to the breakdown of relationships, the parents would be entitled to seek possession from their daughter-in-law, however, for a reasonable period they would have to provide some shelter to the daughter-in-law during which time she is able to seek her remedies against her husband."
17.Perusal of the law on these issue would show that a daughter in law cannot, as a matter of right,
claim any interest or right in the property owned by the father-in- law or the mother-in-law.
However, she has every right to claim the right of residence from her husband.
In case, the relationship of son and parents is not acrimonious and they seem to be colluding with each other to seek eviction of the daughter-in-law then
, both the parents-in-law and the son can be made responsible for providing an alternate accommodation to her.

It is bizarre to file a case against a party for a cause of action which has already been decided and deliberately chosen to have not been executed by the person in whose favor it is passed.

Thus, the evidence put forth only shows that the relationship between plaintiff and defendant no.2 is acrimonious but no evidence has been presented before the Court to suggest a similar state of relationship between the plaintiff and defendant no.1.

On the contrary, the above-stated discussion, based on the admission of the plaintiff would suggest that her relationship with defendant no.1 remains cordial, irrespective of filing of multiple suits against him by her.

19.In any case, the facts appreciated above would not change the admitted status of defendant no.2 of staying with plaintiff in her matrimonial house, which was in possession of the plaintiff, thereby,
making her status as that of a licensee.

Further, the assertion of the defendant no.2 that the suit property was built by defendant no.1 does not help her case as it was a fact alleged by her, thereby putting the onus on her, which even after leading evidence remained inconclusive and irrelevant.

Filing of the present suit by the plaintiff against defendant no.2 results in termination of her license by the plaintiff but considering the evidence lead, it seems that the plaintiff is trying to arm twist the defendant no.2 by misusing the law created for benefit of parents in law who sometimes suffer due to the strenuous relationship with their son and daughter- in-law after marriage.
